questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define cloud computing and dedicated server. (2 marks)

(b) Give THREE advantages of cloud computing has over dedicated server. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Definitions (2 marks)**

- **Cloud computing** is the delivery of computing services (storage, servers, databases, software, processing power) **over the Internet on demand** from the data centres of a provider; the user pays for what is used and does not own or manage the hardware.
- A **dedicated server** is a physical server that is bought or rented and used **exclusively by one organisation**, which hosts its own applications and data on it and manages it.

**(b) Three advantages of cloud computing over a dedicated server (3 marks)**

- **Lower cost**: there is no large initial purchase of hardware and no need for a team to maintain it; the organisation pays only for the resources used.
- **Scalability**: the storage and the processing power can be increased or reduced quickly according to the needs; a dedicated server has a fixed capacity and must be replaced or upgraded.
- **Accessibility and reliability**: the services can be accessed from anywhere with an Internet connection and from any device; the provider takes care of the backups, the updates and the maintenance, and keeps copies of the data in several places.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain each of the following computer crimes and give a method to prevent each:

(a) Hacking. (2 marks)

(b) Spam. (2 marks)

(c) Spyware. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Computer crime | Explanation | Method of prevention |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Hacking** (2 marks) | Gaining **unauthorised access** to a computer system or network, usually to steal, change or destroy data or to use the system illegally. | Use **strong passwords** and a **firewall**; give users access rights; **encrypt** sensitive data; keep the software updated. |
| **(b) Spam** (2 marks) | Sending **unsolicited bulk e-mail** (junk mail), often advertising, fraud or links to malicious programs; it fills the mailboxes and wastes time and bandwidth. | Use a **spam filter**; do not give the e-mail address on public websites; do not answer or open messages from unknown senders and block or report the senders. |
| **(c) Spyware** (2 marks) | A malicious program installed **secretly** on a computer that **monitors the user's activity** (keys typed, websites visited, passwords) and sends the information to another person. | Install and update **anti-spyware / antivirus software**; download programs only from trusted sources; do not click on suspicious links or attachments; use a firewall. |

(b) Explain the functions of the operating System during managing memory. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Completed table**

|---|---|---|
| 1 | Operating system (system software) | Windows, Linux, Android |
| 2 | General purpose (application software) | Word processor (Microsoft Word) or spreadsheet (Microsoft Excel) |
| 3 | Utility software (system software) | Recycler (the recycle bin that stores the deleted files) |
| 4 | Language translator | Compiler, interpreter or assembler (for example the GCC compiler for C) |

**(b) Functions of the operating system in memory management (4 marks)**

- **Allocation and release of memory**: the operating system gives each program the memory space that it needs when it is loaded, and frees this space when the program ends, so that it can be used by other programs.
- **Keeping track of the memory**: it records which parts of the RAM are in use and by which process, and which parts are free.
- **Protection**: it prevents a program from reading or writing in the memory area of another program or of the operating system itself.
- **Virtual memory and swapping**: when the RAM is full, it moves parts of programs (pages) between the RAM and the hard disk, so that several programs can run at the same time (multitasking) even if their total size is larger than the RAM.
